prior rounds 1-11 (recovered from docs/ux-gauntlet/contracts/P8.md, not re-derived): round 1 shipped the merged timeline (/api/history, /api/history/runs/{id}, /api/history/since) beside the five pre-existing /api/versions routes, replacing three disconnected records (#Versions, the settings activity log, the in-memory bell feed) plus a fourth that had never been read (output/run_log.jsonl) with one attributed timeline and a restore path proven to cover the same nine logical files and to snapshot first. AssistantVersions.jsx was deleted once fully replaced (seven capability tests plus a grep proving nothing imports it). Round 2 added history paging (until/before cursor). Round 3 fixed a competitor-boundary breach: GET /api/history?kind=run was serving three rival channels' run rows because operator_channel had gone blank; runs are now withheld tri-state rather than guessed, and a follow-up fix made three surfaces stop printing a zero for an unknown count. Round 4 fixed an empty-window sentence firing for a genuinely non-empty record. Round 5 fixed the same defect class recurring for pruned records (activity_log keeps 5,000 lines, version_store keeps 200 points) by publishing record_starts and retention as real facts. Round 6 fixed the reader's own slice being reported as the store's total size, and reclassified PATCH /api/versions/{id} out of the generic restore bucket into its own action code. Round 7 fixed restore-point diff chips rendering as dumped, indistinguishable, truncated JSON (seven identical-looking restrictions) by giving every store row a real identity, and closed a second competitor-boundary leak where a pin's diff chip carried a channel name inside an engine key. Round 8 fixed the search box reporting nothing-matches when the server-side actor filter two centimetres away found 23 results, by teaching the empty-page state to name what a wider page or an actor filter would reveal. Round 9 fixed refused writes (24.9 percent of recorded requests) rendering as accomplished acts throughout the timeline, the change-tab count and the compliance attestation; outcomes are now tri-state (applied/refused/unknown) end to end. Round 10 closed the restore path as a second door into three company-only settings: a channel-affiliated operator could restore a version file that silently flipped audience_model_activation, moved a regulatory limit and rewrote operator_channel to a rival; file-level permissions are now resolved from each guarded field's own wall (guardrail_store, compliance_api_licence, model_activation) so a restore and a direct write obey one rule. 130+ tests accumulated across the ten test files under the reserved prefix; all documented as passing at each round's close.
